Q: How do I extract an HTML title with Perl? A:

Coming back many years later, things are so much simpler with Mojolicious since it has all the pieces you need, you don't fool around with HTML yourself, and you don't need to figure out the right regex:

$ perl -Mojo -E 'say g(shift)->dom->at("title")->text' https://stackoverflow.com
Newest Questions - Stack Overflow

As a program, that's a little bit more involved:

use v5.10;
use Mojo::UserAgent;

say Mojo::UserAgent->new->get($ARGV[0])->dom->at('title')->text;

This is simply DOM processing. Specify the HTML element you want, then pull out the parts you want (such as the text).

There are more examples in the Mojo::UserAgent docs, as well as my book Mojolicious Web Clients.

Q: Google Sheets VLOOKUP across Mismatched Ranges in Multiple Sheets A:

always when you construct the virtual array with array brackets {} both sides needs to be of the same size.

={A1:A10, B1,B10}

or:

={A1:C10; D1:F10}

in your case, the array literal error comes from mismatched rows when you use "infinite" rows by not specifying the end row. eg. your sheet1 has more or fewer rows then your sheet2 - because that comma in { } stacks your arrays side by side not top to bottom

=INDEX(IF(LEN(B5), VLOOKUP(B5, {SHEET1!A3:B; SHEET2!A15:B}, 2, ), ))

UPDATE:

now possible to use HSTACK and VSTACK:

=INDEX(IF(LEN(B5), VLOOKUP(B5, VSTACK(SHEET1!A3:B, SHEET2!A15:B), 2, ), ))

and arrays do not need to be of same size (width and height wise) anymore!

Q: Can't Import win32gui and win32ui modules to my project on Python 3.8 32-bit A:

if you use conda, let remove current pywin32 and reinstall with conda command

uninstall:pip uninstall pywin32

install with conda: conda install pywin32

maybe you will get error when import win32api solutions: go to conda env directory run post_install command: python Scripts/pywin32_postinstall.py -install

for venv: you can go to venv directory run command like conda python Scripts/pywin32_postinstall.py -install

the above command will copy pywin32 dll(s) file to windows system32 folder

Q: Installing openpyxl in python 2.7 A:

System install of openpyxl may not work in lower Python versions. You can try to install development edition of openpyxl. You can follow the below link to install development edition of Python. This way you won't impact package installs in your machine. https://openpyxl.readthedocs.io/en/2.5/windows-development.html#:~:text=Install%20a%20development%20version%20of,pip%20install%20%2De%20.&text=Releases%20for%20legacy%20versions%20of%20Python%3A&text=0%20for%20Python%202.7

Q: "detail": "CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing or incorrect." A:

Try to add the CSRF token in your template, somewhere in your form :

{% csrf_token %}

See django documentation here.

Q: Unable to read element properties A:

The source properties are coming from source models (i.e. Revit) and are extracted by Model Derivative service - Tandem is using data from this service when populating schema with property details. It seems like there is currently no way to get both global and localized name, unfortunately.

Just to add - I noticed in your example you're referring to Identity Data.Type Name. This is related to element type concept from Revit. Note that Tandem is following this concept. To find out type information to can read QC.FamilyType parameter from element to get related type. You can find example here.
